external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme participant who uses the mobile app and connects partner apps.

external_entities.name: members' phones
external_entities.description: Phones used by members to run the mobile app and retain mobile refresh tokens.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application operated by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application signs members in through the authorization server and calls the rewards API with an access token.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow and then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge. The app keeps a refresh token on the phone. A mobile refresh token never expires: every time the app uses it, its expiry slides forward another ninety days.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The authorization server handles member sign-in, consent, authorization codes, refresh tokens and access-token issuance.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The authorization server signs tokens for the support console with the same key.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API validates access-token signatures and reads and writes the points ledger, including gift-card redemptions.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It does not check which client or which audience a token was issued for. It also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A partner web application that requests tokens and can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
processes.notes: The partnerships team registers each partner app by hand and gives it a client ID and a client secret. The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.

processes.name: browser
processes.description: A member's browser displays the authorization server sign-in and consent screen and returns the authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
processes.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
processes.notes: The member's sign-in on the authorization server is kept in a cookie for thirty days. Nobody decided an idle timeout for it.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_stores.notes: Member refresh tokens remain in the database after an account is closed. Protection at rest was not recorded.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Stores every member's points balance and every points transaction, including the client recorded for each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The ledger records which client made each change, and not which member approved it.
data_stores.notes: Protection at rest was not recorded.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Stores every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_stores.notes: Protection at rest was not recorded.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: authorization code flow
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back.

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: The partner app sends token requests to the authorization server using its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: Every connection from a partner server uses HTTPS.

data_flows.name: sign-in and consent
data_flows.description: The member signs in and approves the consent screen in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes.

data_flows.name: sign-in and consent
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server sign-in and consent page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes.
data_flows.notes: The member's sign-in on the authorization server is kept in a cookie for thirty days.

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: An authorization code stays valid for ten minutes. Every connection from a browser uses HTTPS.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and updates identity and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: read and write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: The connection method was not recorded.

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes received requests and headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_flows.notes: The connection method was not recorded.

data_flows.name: request access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account. It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: The connection method was not recorded. Nothing happens to that member's refresh tokens.
data_flows.data_description: account closure and member identity data

trust_boundaries.description: The system components described as running in the organisation's own cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: Members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud environment.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.basis: The source calls it 'our mobile app' and does not describe it as a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The partner app presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that partner apps are web applications.

assumptions.assumption: The support console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that the support console is a web app.
The source says it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
The source says it is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.basis: It holds member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data.
